- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of decline from peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% per day of reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a “horizon decay” rule — reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after day 7.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment “switch point” as trigger for 1–2% directional adjustment.
